title: Cottage Pie
subtitle: Beef mince in gravy under a mashed-potato top
excerpt: The definitive British mince pie: beef mince cooked with onion, carrot, and Worcestershire sauce in a rich gravy, topped with creamy mashed potato and baked until the top is golden. Freezes perfectly.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cottage pie has been documented in British cooking since the late eighteenth century, when the term referred to the economical use of leftover meat under a potato topping. The shift to fresh minced beef became standard during the nineteenth century as mincing machines became widespread. It is closely related to shepherd's pie, which uses lamb mince; the distinction is firmly kept in British cooking. The dish is one of the most widely eaten home-cooked meals in Britain.

content.text: The mince filling needs to be properly thick before it goes under the potato or the topping will sink and become soggy. Cook it until most of the liquid has evaporated and the mince just holds its shape when you press a spoon into it. The mash should be slightly stiffer than you would serve on its own, so it pipes or spreads without collapsing into the filling.

Heat a large frying pan over high heat. Add the mince and break it up. Cook for 8 minutes until well browned with no pink remaining. Drain off excess fat. Add the onion, carrot, celery, and garlic. Cook for 8 minutes.

Add the tomato puree and flour and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in the wine, then the stock. Add the Worcestershire sauce, thyme, and bay leaves. Season. Simmer for 20 minutes until the sauce is thick. Remove the bay leaves and thyme.
While the mince cooks, boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes until tender. Drain well and mash with the butter and milk. Season generously. The mash should be thick and smooth.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Spoon the mince filling into the baking dish. Spread or pipe the mash over the top in an even layer and rough up the surface with a fork. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the top is golden and the filling is bubbling at the edges.
